item: storage_events.end's tombstone trim keeps its loop's back-edge inside the lock (R163)
status: shipped (local, applies on a tree that has Q's follow-on 0b2c4917a)
summary: storage_events.end trims the tombstone memory (_ENDED) in a loop under _LOCK, and scripts/analytics45_seed.py reaches it on the main thread (kv_set_json -> write_lock -> WriterGate.release -> _note_hold_end -> end). The loop is now while True with the bound test first, so its back-edge is inside the with on CPython 3.13 and an interrupt delivered there cannot leave _LOCK owned. Q wrote the pair; here the code and its new test file go in one commit. The dis test (Q's _uncovered_loop_heads, in tests/test_gates_survive_an_interrupt.py) is red with the old loop; a behaviour test pins that the tombstone memory still forgets the oldest keys first and stops at its bound.
